title: Maximum Value of an Ordered Triplet II
summary: Given an integer array nums, find the maximum value of (nums[i] - nums[j]) * nums[k] for all indices i < j < k.
statement: Given an integer array nums, find the maximum value of (nums[i] - nums[j]) * nums[k] for all indices i < j < k. If no such triplet exists, return 0.
constraints: nums contains at least three positive integers.
Return the maximum value, or zero when every triplet value is negative.
reference_solution:
def maximum_ordered_triplet_value(nums):
    best_value=0;best_prefix=nums[0];best_difference=0
    for value in nums[1:]:
        best_value=max(best_value,best_difference*value)
        best_difference=max(best_difference,best_prefix-value)
        best_prefix=max(best_prefix,value)
    return best_value
hints: At k, only the best earlier difference nums[i]-nums[j] matters.
Scan once while maintaining the largest prefix value and largest valid difference before using the current value as k.
Update answer first, then difference, then prefix maximum to preserve index order.
Each state uses only earlier indices at the moment it contributes, and retains the maximum sufficient statistic for every future multiplication.
editorial: Each state uses only earlier indices at the moment it contributes, and retains the maximum sufficient statistic for every future multiplication.

tests.explanation: Indices zero, two, and four give (12-1)*7=77.
Indices one, two, and four give (10-3)*19=133.
